title: The purl stitch
subtitle: The reverse of the knit stitch and the second pillar of knitted fabric.
excerpt: The purl stitch (abbreviated p) produces the horizontal bump that sits on the wrong side of stocking stitch. Every knitter learns it second, after the knit stitch, and it opens the door to ribbing, seed stitch, and all textured knitting.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, Series 1 (1886). Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938). Beeton's Book of Needlework (1870).

glossaryTerms.definition: The reverse of the knit stitch. Produced by inserting the needle into the stitch from right to left through the front, wrapping the yarn clockwise, and drawing the loop back through. Abbreviated p.
The back face of a piece of flat knitting, typically the purl side of stocking stitch. Abbreviated WS.

content.text: (abbreviated p) is the knit stitch worked in reverse. Where the knit stitch draws the new loop backward through the stitch, the purl stitch draws it forward. The result is the same loop seen from the other side: a horizontal bump that sits on the

of stocking stitch, and which is brought to the front in ribbing, seed stitch (UK: moss stitch), and reverse stocking stitch panels. Most knitters find the purl stitch slightly slower and more effortful than the knit; this is normal and evens out with practice. Difficulty: beginner.
DK yarn and 4 mm needles with a few rows of garter stitch already worked (or a fresh cast-on)
Bring the working yarn to the front of the work, between the two needles.
Insert the right needle tip into the first stitch on the left needle from right to left, entering through the front of the stitch. The right needle is now in front of the left.
Wrap the working yarn anticlockwise around the right needle tip, passing between the two needle tips.
Draw the right needle backward through the stitch, bringing the new loop back through.
Slip the old stitch off the left needle. One purl stitch completed.

Continental style: hold the yarn in the left hand, insert the right needle into the stitch from right to left, then scoop the yarn forward and through. Many knitters find Continental purling faster once the motion is automatic, though the wrist turn takes practice.

Every flat pattern alternates knit and purl rows on the wrong side of stocking stitch. Ribbing is knit and purl stitches in alternating columns. Seed stitch (UK: moss stitch) sets purl stitches over knit columns and vice versa. Cables are knit panels set against reverse stocking stitch purl backgrounds.

items.symptom: Yarn sits at the back when it should be at the front at the start of a purl row
items.cause: Forgetting to bring the yarn forward before the first stitch
items.fix: Always check yarn position before the first stitch of every row. Purl rows start with yarn in front; knit rows start with yarn behind.

items.symptom: Purl stitches are noticeably looser than knit stitches
items.cause: The purl wrap naturally releases more yarn than the knit wrap in English-style knitting
items.fix: Consciously snug each purl stitch by pulling the right-hand yarn a little after completing the wrap. The tension will even out. Continental purlers rarely have this problem.

items.symptom: Extra stitches appear at the beginning of a purl row
items.cause: Yarn brought forward before the needle is inserted, then accidentally wrapped over the needle to form an extra loop
items.fix: Bring the yarn forward before inserting the needle, not after. The yarn position at step 1 must be confirmed before step 2.
